inputs.text: Health workers in Nigeria are standing up for their rights and the future of public care, as tensions in the sector boiled over on Thursday when members of the Joint Health Sector Unions and the Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations marched through Abuja to protest these controversial reform bills in the National Assembly. Gathering at the Unity Fountain in Maitama, they made clear their opposition to legislation that looks set to further entrench inequality by weakening labor protections and shifting priorities away from the needs of ordinary people. This kind of push from the top often serves institutional interests over the vulnerable, deepening historical divides in access to healthcare and leaving frontline staff and the communities they serve more exposed to exploitation and neglect. It's a vital reminder that real reform must come from protecting workers and fighting structural injustice, not imposing changes that benefit the powerful at everyone's expense.
